question: Should OpenClaw adopt this generic `ChannelLoginMethod` contract and shared Chrome WhatsApp socket identity as the canonical phone-code implementation?
rationale: The feature is useful and the patch is technically coherent, but landing it permanently expands the public Plugin SDK, changes a shared WhatsApp runtime default, tightens persisted-auth interpretation, and requires choosing between two candidate PRs.

options.title: Adopt this branch after rebase
options.body: Accept the narrow discriminated login-method API, refresh against current main, and require exact-head dual-flow proof if maintainers want additional dependency confidence.

options.title: Keep phone-code WhatsApp-local
options.body: Avoid the new public SDK contract and expose the helper through a WhatsApp-owned setup or command surface instead.

options.title: Adopt the older proven branch
options.body: Repair and rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85866 if maintainers prefer its implementation and physical-device proof.

recommendation.title: Adopt this branch after rebase
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow discriminated login-method API, refresh against current main, and require exact-head dual-flow proof if maintainers want additional dependency confidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects steipete most directly to the channel auth CLI, Plugin SDK boundary, and WhatsApp login surface that define the permanent public contract.
